Topic at a glance
RFCTLARR Act, 2013 — Social Impact Assessment (ss. 4–9), Preliminary Notification (s. 11), Declaration (s. 19) is a registered act in Land Laws. RFCTLARR Act, 2013 — Social Impact Assessment (ss. 4–9), Preliminary Notification (s. 11), Declaration (s. 19) is governed by Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013; Transfer of Property Act, 1882; State land laws and constitutional property protection under Article 300A. identify the acquisition notification, applicable statute, land category, consent or urgency route, award date, possession and the limitation or objection stage.

Provenance, purpose and doctrinal foundation
The topic exists to organise a legally enforceable rule, doctrine or professional procedure. Read the statutory text, constitutional setting, institutional purpose and binding authorities together. The correct analysis begins with the legal question and avoids replacing the governing enactment with a generic textbook summary.

Textual anatomy and operative test
1. Identify the governing enactment, section, article, rule, doctrine or professional standard named by the topic.
2. Deconstruct definitions, conditions precedent, exceptions, provisos, explanations, jurisdictional limits and remedies.
3. Distinguish the topic from its nearest neighbour: RFCTLARR Act, 2013 — Determination of Market Value (s. 26) & Solatium (s. 30); Rehabilitation and Resettlement Award under Chapter V (ss. 31–42).
4. Apply the rule to the record and state which fact satisfies or fails each ingredient.

Courtroom and evidentiary roadmap
Competent forum: the Collector, land-acquisition authority, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority, civil court where jurisdiction survives, High Court under Article 226 and Supreme Court according to the statutory route. the acquiring authority must establish public purpose, statutory notice, hearing, valuation, award and rehabilitation compliance; affected persons prove title, possession, dependency and compensation claims from the record. Where electronic records are relied upon, apply BSA 2023 s. 63 and the applicable burden provisions without treating electronic admissibility as proof of the ultimate fact. Identify limitation, notice, maintainability, alternative remedy and the exact relief sought.
